status_vocabulary.confirmed: pre-registered, OpenTimestamps-stamped blind confirmatory run; protocol and pass/fail fixed before data
status_vocabulary.measured: one or more runs with a committed receipt in this repo; not blind-confirmed
status_vocabulary.measured-private: a run whose receipt exists only in the private audit tree; a reader of this repo cannot check it
status_vocabulary.retired: was published, now known wrong; kept so the retraction is findable
status_vocabulary.superseded: true as measured, but a later entry is the number to quote
status_vocabulary.open: a question the docs raise that has no evidence either way

claims.claim: The fused NF4 grouped GEMM (fp32 accumulate, bf16 epilogue) has never measured less accurate than the dequantize-to-bf16-then-GEMM baseline, in every confirmatory cell.
claims.notes: PORTABILITY.md records this as TF32-specific; it is a CUDA-tensor-core statement, not a vendor-independent one.

claims.claim: Fused J/token is below the dequant baseline in 104 of 112 confirmatory-grade cells across v1-v3; six of the eight misses are the top_k=1 / tiny-shape class.
claims.hardware: sm_86, two devices, n=3 fresh-process reps

claims.claim: At batch-1 decode on sm_86, census MoE shapes (OLMoE, Qwen3-30B, Gemma-4, gpt-oss-120b) run 1.16-2.73x the dequant baseline at median; top_k=1 and tiny (<~5M weight elements) shapes are known losers.
claims.notes: gpt-oss `down` 2880x2880 is instance-sensitive (0.7-2.0x across five instances). measured_on is the last confirmatory run the entry cites (v6, 2026-07-14); the 1.16-2.73x band is stated in the v3 receipt (2026-07-13).

claims.claim: Head-to-head against Unsloth's own MoE grouped-GEMM kernel, same pod and process, in the 4-bit-storage regime: decode 1.70x on H100 (their TMA path live) and 2.79x on RTX 4090; J/token 2.51x and 3.32x better. Unsloth wins its own bf16-resident regime by 2.6-5.3x at prefill on the H100.
claims.notes: Forward pass only; the training-axis leg is exploratory and licenses no claim. The model-level, training-axis end-to-end head-to-head is registered in experts4bit-qlora as e4b.train.h2h.unsloth.qwen3.5090.2026-09-05 (2026-09-05, one RTX 5090, Qwen3-30B-A3B: experts4bit-qlora 1.522 s/step vs Unsloth 2.151, ratio 1.413; held-out loss comparable at N=60; at N=200 Unsloth's held-out loss is lower, 0.2713 vs 0.2881). That is a different level and regime, so it does not supersede this kernel-level claim. measured_on is the receipt's publication commit (2026-08-12; the receipt states no run date, and amendment 2 of the protocol was registered 2026-08-12T23:20Z).

claims.claim: SUPERSEDED: the grouped-bf16-GEMM execution class (tgale96's grouped_gemm, dequant in the timed path) loses to the fused kernel on every census cell, decode median 4.67x.
claims.notes: That backend never executed Unsloth's own kernel and the proxy is 1.33x slower than the real thing; the number was measured against a weaker opponent than the label implied. Kept because the README still quotes it, with the caveat.

claims.claim: At the Qwen3-30B-A3B serving cell (E=128, top-8, B=16) on an RTX 5090, gemm_4bit_grouped runs the routed expert GEMM in 0.42 / 0.21 ms where torch._grouped_mm on unquantised bf16 takes 0.88-1.30 ms: 2.1-6.0x across two boxes, on half the weight bytes.
claims.notes: measured_on is the receipt's commit date (PR #299, 2026-08-29); the receipt states no run date and ran on main 4f1db333 (2026-08-28), so the run falls on 2026-08-28/29. Recorded as '2026-08' until 0.30.2.

claims.claim: Against a CUDA-graphed per-expert baseline at the decode band (T=32) the fused path LOSES on both 4090 and H100 (0.949x, 0.858x); the memory-traffic win survives only at training shape on bandwidth-limited cards (1.489x on the 4090, parity 1.059x on the H100).
claims.notes: The README states this. Any 'fused wins at decode' reading that ignores graphing is wrong. measured_on is the first commit of the leg-4 receipt that carries all four numbers (2026-08-13; it states no run date); the graphed-buckets receipt is the later 2026-08-15 re-race and supplies none of them.

claims.claim: Inside a real OLMoE QLoRA finetune, fused vs the per-expert loop runs 4.50x on a 4090 and 4.75x on an H100 on real prose; random token ids understate it at 2.75x / 2.81x because prose routes to 98.4% of experts (cv 0.687) where random ids hit 87.5% (cv 1.463).
claims.notes: Baseline is e4b's own per-expert loop, not CUDA-graphed; peak VRAM does not improve. Random token ids understate the kernel by ~1.6x (4.50/2.75, 4.75/2.81); benchmark on real text.

claims.claim: dgrad_4bit_grouped is the training backward in one launch: gate_up E=256 5.92 ms vs 61.78 ms for the per-expert loop, down 3.28 vs 85.12 ms (A2000, T_cat=4096); one training step at E=256 goes 403.7 to 26.5 ms. On by default since 0.9.1; gradient lands ~2.9e-3 from the exact loop, inside the bf16 budget.

evidence.note: the A2000 cells (gate_up 5.92 vs 61.78 ms, down 3.28 vs 85.12 ms, the composed step 403.7 -> 26.5 ms) are recorded in the 0.7.0 release entry; no kernel/RESULTS-*.md carries them, which the earlier glob implied

claims.notes: measured_on is the date of the 0.7.0 entry that records the A2000 cells, and the run date the dgrad-gate receipt states.

claims.claim: Every kernel that scales an expert id or a block-table row by a stride computes the base offset in int64: the 10 boundary cases of kernel/test_expert_offset_boundary.py -- five below-boundary controls in-process and five above-boundary cases in fresh processes, for the NF4 decode GEMV (scalar, split-K, wide-load, dot-pad), the NF4 M-tile and dgrad, the MXFP4 GEMM / GEMV / gemv_mxfp4_b32, the int4-b32 GEMV and M-tile, and the fp8 paged decode kernels -- pass against the pure-torch references on an RTX 5090, closing #87 by observation (PR #342).
claims.unit: boundary cases passed, above 2^31 in fresh processes
claims.conditions: N=256, K=1024 (2^17 B per expert; experts 16383 | 16384; E=16386, 2.00 GiB packed + scales); dot-pad at its census shape N=1536, K=2048 (experts 1365 | 1366; E=1368); fp8 paged attention head_dim 128, 8 kv heads, 16 tokens/block, K rows padded to a 1 MiB stride (rows 2047 | 2048; 2050 rows, 2.00 GiB K pool); about 2.3 GiB of device memory per case, skipped below 4 GiB free
claims.notes: The public evidence is the test and the 0.30.1 changelog entry; the GPU log (10 passed in 29.07 s) is in the private receipt tree, so the run itself cannot be checked from this repository -- rerun the file on any CUDA device with >= 4 GiB free. Same release, #324: an infeasible tile is refused or re-dispatched before the launch (_triton_shim.UnsupportedShapeError, fp8_paged_attn.packed_unsupported, nf4_grouped.prefill_fit) instead of surfacing Triton's OutOfResources; no NVIDIA configuration moves and no registered number changes, so it carries no entry of its own. On the same 5090 run kernel/test_shape_feasibility.py passed compiled and under the interpreter (28 each) and the fp8 paged modes passed (47; the 37 f32 modes stay deselected under #319), with the packed-tile fallback firing at head_dim 256 / 8 kv heads.

claims.claim: The certified single-stream decode anchor for Qwen3-30B-A3B on the RTX 5090 class is 7.37 ms/step +-4.2%, about 130-142 tok/s, with the class carrying 8.5% inter-box dispersion while each box repeats to 0.16%.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), three rented boxes, A/A pairs

claims.claim: GNF4_GEMV_DOTPAD and GNF4_ATTN_COMPUTE=fp8 ship ON by default (capability-conditional): 8192 teacher-forced tokens through the paged decode path, both knobs 7.843 -> 6.803 ms/step at delta-ppl -0.0021 against a +-0.05 bar. The fp8 path asserts sm_89+, v_groups==1, k_groups in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16); unset env falls back to f32 where fp8 cannot run, an explicit fp8 request is never downgraded.
claims.notes: Read the ppl deltas as zero, not gains. Dispatch receipts (dispatch_counts, compute_counts) exist because an env var is a request, not an event. Correction (0.30.2, 2026-09-05): the sentence said `k_groups in (1,2,4)`, the predicate as it stood at the 2026-08-27 run; fp8_paged_attn.fp8_compute_unsupported has admitted (1, 2, 4, 8, 16) since 0.26.0 (Gemma-4's per-layer key-scale groups) and the sentence now describes the shipped predicate. The measurement and its numbers are unchanged.

claims.claim: fp8_paged_decode_attention takes window (sliding), sinks (per-head logit in the softmax denominator, the gpt-oss s_aux convention), sm_scale, and k_row_bytes/v_row_bytes stride overrides in all four decode kernels; 35/35 fp8-mode GPU tests on an RTX 5090 (torch 2.8.0+cu128, triton 3.4.0); bytes and arithmetic for window=0, sinks=None unchanged.
claims.notes: End-to-end parity of the SERVING path built on these (Granite, gpt-oss, Gemma-4) is measured in experts4bit-qlora's receipts, which are private -- see e4b's register.

claims.claim: OPEN: the f32 compute modes (split, packed) of the fp8 paged decode miss their reference by up to 0.074 (tol 0.02) on 10 of 35 tests on torch 2.8.0+cu128 / triton 3.4.0 (sm_120), on unmodified main; the fp8 modes -- the sm_120 serving default -- pass.
claims.notes: Serving on sm_120 with GNF4_ATTN_COMPUTE unset is unaffected. The f32 path is the sm_80-sm_88 default (sm_89+, Hopper included, defaults to fp8 where fp8_compute_unsupported passes), the fallback wherever an fp8 constraint fails, and every explicit f32 request on any card; its tests cannot gate a lane on these boxes with -x. docs/capabilities.json carries it as fp8-paged-attention-f32-compute, status unsupported, until this closes.

claims.claim: The uniform int4-b32 decode GEMV (int8 activations, exact integer accumulation) reaches 1,044 GB/s dense at M=1 on the 5090, 6.9-7.2x over the NF4 register-LUT GEMV; grouped top-8 cells 3.8-4.3x. The grouped M-tile int4 GEMM runs gate_up 1.947x / down 4.500x over the NF4 grouped kernel at the B=16 census cells.
claims.notes: Measured refusals kept: the format stays OFF the lm_head (+0.18 ppl) and dense attention shapes lose to bf16 in both the GEMV and M=16 GEMM regimes. measured_on is the date of the 0.18.0 entry that first quotes these cells -- an upper bound, since the run dates are in the private receipts (INT4B16/P1, P15-B16), not stated publicly.

HessianAccumulator stores off-device (0.23.0) so Mixtral's 128 projections fit.

claims.claim: Qwen3-235B-A22B with all NF4 experts in ~128 GB pinned host RAM streams at 5.57 tok/s = 102-103% of the measured 44.3 GB/s link's waterfall ceiling on a 13.6 GB working set (synthetic weights, real attention + router); the dequant path on the identical pipeline: 1.81 tok/s.

The real 438 GB Qwen3-235B checkpoint, stream-quantised to NF4, generates coherent greedy text at 4.3-4.4 tok/s on 15.2 GB VRAM across five pods at 45-55 GB/s links; per-token time follows t ~= c_box + bytes/link with c_box measured 53.5-114.0 ms across seven hosts. A fixed fraction-of-waterfall is NOT the law (retired 2026-07-22).
claims.hardware: five rented pods; gen4 desktop L40S 2.6 tok/s; gen5 bare-metal H100 PCIe 3.9
claims.notes: measured_on is the gen5 bare-metal leg that supplies the seven-host c_box band (receipts-gen5-20260722; the run log starts 2026-07-23T00:06Z, 2026-07-22 local); the five-pod Phase B receipt is 2026-07-14.

claims.claim: Expert prefetch is CLOSED, negative, over four registered arcs: stickiness 0.44 (B2); the pre-attention router predicts the post-attention top-8 at 0.93 but the win does not land (B3); threaded issuance 0.57x (B4); zero-copy speculative gather loses by the (2-H)x bytes law, break-even needs H >~ 0.95 (B5). Recommended copy path is --prefetch-mode gpu (UVA gather), +1.5% on one host.

The NVMe tier is a batch tier: at the measured per-box S ~= 3.45 GB/s a fully cold 235B streams ~2.3 s/token and a K3-class model ~7.5 s/token. What it buys is reachability and provenance, not latency.
claims.unit: GB/s sustained read at 13-50 MiB requests, QD>=4
claims.hardware: QNAP Xeon W-1250, FireCuda 530 on PCIe Gen3 x4
claims.notes: measured_on is the S curve run (docs/nvme-ceilings.md, 2026-07-27 evening); the concurrent-with-PCIe leg and the determinism receipt followed on 2026-07-28.

claims.claim: int4_b32._plan takes the activation-row count R and the SM count: for R >= 16 on parts with <= 64 SMs, split-K is sized so about 8 blocks per SM are resident and collapses to sk = 1 (no reduce launch) where the grid alone covers that; below R = 16 the plan is exactly the previous N-only rule on every SM count. Measured on an RTX A2000 (26 SMs; CUDA-graph replay; full cost including reduce_partials) over 48 cells -- qwen3_moe / granitemoe / olmoe gate_up + down at R = 1..128: the N-only rule costs 1.136x the per-cell optimum, the R-aware rule 1.011x, never slower than the N-only rule on any cell; 1.102x at R = 16 rising to 1.145x at R = 128 summed over the six shapes.
claims.unit: x the per-cell optimum over 48 cells (the N-only rule: 1.136x)
claims.conditions: kernel-level GEMV timings at a fixed row count, not step-level; the 8 x sm_count target is measured on sm_86 only and the term is gated to sm_count <= 64 (SPLITK_R_TERM_MAX_SMS) after a 5090 step-level read of 1.0064 / 1.0063 NEW/OLD at B=16 (experts4bit-qlora#533, P39); mxfp4_grouped.gemv_mxfp4_b32 deliberately keeps the N-only plan (its own 32-cell sweep, bench/int4/mx_sweep.py, regressed 2 cells by 15-17%)
claims.notes: measured_on is the receipt's commit date (PR #357, 2026-09-10); the RESULTS file states no run date. B=1 decode calls the grouped GEMV at R = top_k (4 or 8 for every shipped MoE), so SPLITK_R_FLOOR = 16 leaves every B=1 cell and the licensed serve configuration untouched by construction; kernel/test_int4_b32.py pins R < 16 to a verbatim copy of the old rule, re-derives the worst-cell bound (SK_R_BOUND 1.07; measured 1.064x, granitemoe/down at R = 16) from the receipts, and fails if a shipped model routes to >= 16 experts. sm_count enters the plan, so bitwise equality across boxes must pin sk rather than plan it; within a box the plan is a pure function of (N, K, R).

claims.claim: K14 (pre-registered): at M=16 no shipped int4 arm beats the bf16 dequant-then-GEMM path on Qwen3-30B-A3B's four attention projections -- the grouped int4 GEMM at the best of twelve swept block configurations is 1.12-2.00x slower, the int4 GEMV 1.46-2.40x slower -- so the registered mix saving over 48 layers is 0.000 ms/step against a 0.5 ms bar: REFUTED. q_proj's bf16 path reads 16.78 MB in 10.35 us (106% of the measured 1528 GB/s streaming ceiling); k_proj / v_proj are launch-bound at 1.74x the 3.57 us floor.
claims.unit: ms/step mix saving at M=16 over 48 layers (registered bar 0.5)
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120, 170 SMs), torch 2.8.0+cu128 / triton 3.4.0, rented host
claims.notes: Prediction 1 (gemm wins on q/o_proj) REFUTED at 1.205x / 1.123x slower; predictions 2 (GEMV_ROWS_MAX = 1 is right) and 3 (k/v launch-bound within 2x of the floor) CONFIRMED. The A2000 dry-run read 0.898 / 1.035 on the same cells -- an sm_86 number does not transfer to sm_120, the rule P39 established. Two bounds the lane did not go looking for, arithmetic under a stated assumption rather than measurements: o_proj runs at 60% of ceiling against q_proj's 106% on the same bytes (about 0.38 ms/step if matched, on the bf16 side), and unfused q/k/v spend three launches where one would do (about 0.44 ms/step at the ceiling). A roofline int4 projection kernel would be worth about 1.29 ms/step; nothing shipped realises it (the kernel built for that arithmetic reaches 22% of the bandwidth it would need). Cost $0.0653 against a $1.50 lane ceiling. Cross-check: the four projections sum to 1.977 ms/step, within 5% of experts4bit-qlora's P42 census share for the same 192 launches.

claims.claim: K15 (pre-registered): vLLM 0.28.0's Marlin GPTQ kernel at g128 runs Qwen3-30B-A3B's q_proj in 6.37 us and o_proj in 8.28 us at M=16 on the same RTX 5090 where this package's bf16 dequant path takes 10.3 / 16.5 us (1.62x / 1.99x) and its best int4 arm 12.5 / 18.9 us; at matched bytes (g32) Marlin still wins (8.18 / 8.24 us), so the advantage is the kernel, not the weight format. Substituting Marlin where measured saves 0.583-0.812 ms/step, inside the 0.5-1.0 ms band the pre-registration fixed as INCONCLUSIVE; experts4bit-qlora#564's 1.67 ms estimate is refuted as too optimistic (Marlin runs at 34-50% of the streaming ceiling, not at it).
claims.unit: x faster than this package's bf16 dequant path on o_proj at M=16 (q_proj 1.62x)
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120, 170 SMs), driver 595.84; this package in torch 2.8.0+cu128, Marlin in its own venv (vllm 0.28.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130); rented host
claims.notes: Engines as shipped, across different torch/CUDA builds in different processes, as the pre-registration said; adopting Marlin itself (a GPTQ repack, a dependency, a quality gate) is not established here. k_proj / v_proj are unmeasured: MarlinWorkspace was sized N//64 x 16 = 128 for N=512, below the 170-SM count the kernel requires (fixed in #363; the lane ran out of budget before a box used it). Relative error 0.0000-0.0005 against Marlin's own dequantised reference. Cost $1.1253 against a $1.00 lane ceiling -- over by $0.13, closed rather than extended; four of the six rentals were host draws that failed.

claims.claim: K16 (pre-registered 2026-09-18): the small-M int4-b32 GEMM int4_smallm.gemm_int4_b32_smallm (in-register int4 dequantisation, per-32-block scaling inside the tile, bf16 tensor-core MMA over K chunks of 128-256, split-K with the reduction fused into the launch) at M=16 on Qwen3-30B-A3B's attention projections on the RTX 5090: q_proj 6.35 us (this package's bf16 dequant path 10.37, K14's grouped GEMM 12.56), k_proj 4.37 (6.23), v_proj 4.49 (6.29), o_proj 6.39 (18.61, K14 20.73); launch floor 4.61 us. P1 (within 1.4x of Marlin g128, <= 8.9 / 11.6 us) HOLDS at 1.00x / 0.77x of K15's Marlin rows; P2 (beats the bf16 path on q/o) HOLDS; P3 (k/v within 1.2x of bf16) HOLDS; P4 (single-scale control) NOT TESTED -- the bench carried no control arm; P5 (>= 0.4 ms/step at B=16 once routed) HOLDS in the consumer (experts4bit-qlora lane k16-p5, bench/k16/RESULTS-k16-p5.md, 2026-09-19): the bf16 GEMM family carrying the attention projections falls 2.35 ms/step and this kernel costs 1.30 in its place, the timed B=16 step 12.25 -> 11.19 ms (-1.06, -8.6%); the consumer's route defaults to auto from 0.36.2.
claims.unit: x faster than this package's bf16 dequant path on o_proj at M=16 (q_proj 1.63x)
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120, 170 SMs), torch 2.8.0+cu128 / triton 3.4.0, rented host (vast instance 51522950)
claims.notes: Decision rule applied: P1 and P2 hold, so the consumer route is opened (experts4bit-qlora#578, opt-in E4B_ATTN_INT4_SMALLM=1; P5 read 2026-09-19 in the consumer: HOLDS, and experts4bit-qlora 0.36.2 makes the route the default when this package (>= 0.32.0) is installed) and this row is `measured`, not a model-level claim. Every best config is BLOCK_N=32 / 4 warps; q_proj takes SK=1 at KC=256, k/v SK=4, o_proj SK=8 -- the split follows K/N. The A2000 pilot read 2.21x / 2.41x on q/o where the 5090 reads 1.63x / 2.91x: an sm_86 ratio does not transfer to sm_120 in either direction. Relative error 0.0029-0.0033 against the bf16 reference (contract <= 2^-7). Run 1 of the lane (k16-5090) was a HARNESS_ERROR (no pytest on the image) with no number; cost of both draws about $0.06 against the $0.65 lane ceiling. Marlin comparator figures are cross-process, cross-build, biased in Marlin's favour per the standing correction (K15).
